receipt.public_excerpt: Sora is trained on and subsequently generates videos within this compressed latent space. We also train a corresponding decoder model that maps generated latents back to pixel space.

evidence_items.explanation: Sora's output is latent video decoded to pixels. Nothing in it is an explicit object or scene representation.

receipt.public_excerpt: These properties emerge without any explicit inductive biases for 3D, objects, etc.—they are purely phenomena of scale.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI says Sora has no explicit object or 3D structure. This matches 'not segmentations of the world into objects'.

receipt.public_excerpt: The version of Sora we are deploying has many limitations. It often generates unrealistic physics and struggles with complex actions over long durations.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI itself admits the public version often produces unrealistic physics. This supports 'unreliable at that'.

evidence_items.locator: section Emerging simulation capabilities, Long-range coherence and object permanence

receipt.public_excerpt: We find that Sora is often, though not always, able to effectively model both short- and long-range dependencies. For example, our model can persist people, animals and objects even when they are occluded or leave the frame.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI claims some implicit object persistence. This is partial, and it is not an explicit object segmentation, so it does not undercut the claim.

unresolved_gaps: No independent quantitative test of Sora Turbo's physical consistency was cited. 'Unreliable' rests on OpenAI's own admission.
